searchText: im commenting on what you said. i have generated all the era1 files from a full node, you should not need an archive node I am assuming I would need to enable the setting Ryan mentioned. Thank you for the knowledge, that is really nice to know instead of trying to sync an archival node 😁. you won't need to enable that bc era generation is done by iterating over blocks individually Oh really damn I could generate all of them now then that is so nice!. I finished dumping all the era1 files - To store all of era1 it takes 428Gb of storage. - The biggest individual era1 file is epoch 1816 and it takes 642Mb of storage - It took 13h10m22.571641988s to dump all 15,532,032 blocks We are going to host it on some sub-domain at ethportal.net so I will post a link when that is ready I will see if I can host them on a google drive in the meantime <https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1D-GXfX0lRFURzLBwMWfDt5xizbxQJSyy?usp=sharing> here is a google drive link with them till that is setup ~~(still uploading so not all are there yet)~~ BTW RE: > Question RE: 2) I'm curious how the clients that don't include the state root in pre-byzantium receipts actually handle serving devp2p GetReceipts requests for those. I just synced a `reth` node locally to an early block (284957) and hacked up their `manual-p2p` example to send it a `GetReceipts` query for that block, and it looks like it's probably responding w/o the `root`, I'll confirm further before opening an issue upstream, I think at a minimum it should probably not respond for pre-byzantium receipts vs. sending back invalid responses, since IIUC this could lead to clients getting wrong receipt roots when syncing from it. I know this is a bit off-topic now but figured it was a rabbit hole worth pursuing 🙂

excerpts.author: ryanleeschneider
excerpts.content:
BTW RE: 

> Question RE: 2) I'm curious how the clients that don't include the state root in pre-byzantium receipts actually handle serving devp2p GetReceipts requests for those.

I just synced a `reth` node locally to an early block (284957) and hacked up their `manual-p2p` example to send it a `GetReceipts` query for that block, and it looks like it's probably responding w/o the `root`, I'll confirm further before opening an issue upstream, I think at a minimum it should probably not respond for pre-byzantium receipts vs. sending back invalid responses, since IIUC this could lead to clients getting wrong receipt roots when syncing from it.  I know this is a bit off-topic now but figured it was a rabbit hole worth pursuing 🙂
